html:
In the winter of 2009 to 2010 a severe dzud struck Mongolia and killed about a fifth of the country's livestock, millions of animals.

A dzud is a disaster of the steppe in which herds starve or freeze in winter. There are several kinds: deep snow that buries the grass, ice that seals it, or a dry winter with no snow for water. The 2009 to 2010 dzud came after a summer drought left little grass and hay; then came deep snow and long weeks of extreme cold.

Mongolia's herders had grown in number after the end of communism, when collective herds were split up among families, and many had no reserves. Thousands of families lost everything. Many gave up herding and moved to Ulaanbaatar, settling in the felt tents of the city's growing ger districts. Dzuds have long shaped the life of steppe nomads, and scientists link their recent frequency to climate change.
sum: In the winter of 2009 to 2010 a severe dzud struck Mongolia and killed about a fifth of the country's livestock, millions of animals.
